title: Design staged disaster recovery exercises
question: Given a recovery claim, which test form can produce the needed evidence without exceeding the authorized disruption?
scenario: The team wants to prove a payment service's four-hour RTO without interrupting production. The parallel test can restore a copy, but production and recovery share the same identity provider.
focalRelation: recovery claim --required evidence--> exercise objective objective plus maturity/safety --select--> read-through/walkthrough/simulation/parallel/full interruption exercise form --creates bounded evidence and production effect--> result stop criteria --limit--> harm excluded dependency --remains explicit--> assurance gap

states.title: Case facts fixed
states.caption: The team wants to prove a payment service's four-hour RTO without interrupting production. The parallel test can restore a copy, but production and recovery share the same identity provider.

states.title: Controlling condition identified
states.caption: A low-impact exercise can reveal governance and documentation gaps but cannot prove production failover.

states.title: Tempting shortcut rejected
states.caption: A tabletop proves the DR plan will restore systems. It can expose decision, role, communication, and assumption gaps, but it does not prove technical restoration or capacity.

states.title: Bounded action applied
states.caption: State that the test proves restoration procedure and some capacity, not independence from identity failure. Define a parallel scope, use synthetic or approved data, coordinate the provider and business observer, record communications and timing, and create a follow-up test for the shared identity dependency.

states.title: Outcome accepted with limits
states.caption: Given a recovery plan and risk boundary, select an exercise form, define objectives and participants, and communicate test status without overstating what the exercise proves. The case record retains the scope, owner, exceptions, and evidence used for this conclusion.

variants.label: Changed case
variants.changedFact: A service owner requests a full-interruption test during the busiest business day because the team is available.

states.title: Changed case fact isolated
states.caption: A service owner requests a full-interruption test during the busiest business day because the team is available.

states.title: Decision recomputed
states.caption: Reject the timing, select a safer staged or parallel exercise, define an approved full-interruption objective and window, and require business and safety authority. Exercise convenience does not justify uncontrolled business, safety, or customer impact.

states.title: Changed outcome verified
states.caption: The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

prediction.prompt: Given a recovery claim, which test form can produce the needed evidence without exceeding the authorized disruption?

options.label: State that the test proves restoration procedure and some capacity
options.feedback: Correct for this scenario: this answer uses the displayed relation and preserves its scope. It can expose decision, role, communication, and assumption gaps, but it does not prove technical restoration or capacity.

options.label: A tabletop proves the DR plan will restore systems.
options.feedback: Incorrect: It can expose decision, role, communication, and assumption gaps, but it does not prove technical restoration or capacity.

options.label: Meeting four hours in a parallel restore proves the production RTO even though recovery shares the identity provider.
options.feedback: Incorrect: the exercise did not test the shared identity failure or full production conditions. State the tested scope, dependency gap, timing evidence, residual uncertainty, and next exercise needed.

prediction.hint: Name the controlling relationship and the point where its result must be enforced; do not rely on a label or successful prior step.

transfer.prompt: A service owner requests a full-interruption test during the busiest business day because the team is available.

options.label: Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged
options.feedback: Changed fact: A service owner requests a full-interruption test during the busiest business day because the team is available. Why this answer fails: “Reuse the original conclusion because the overall control family is unchanged” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: State that the test proves restoration procedure and some capacity, not independence from identity failure. Repair target: Decision recomputed — Reject the timing, select a safer staged or parallel exercise, define an approved full-interruption objective and window, and require business and safety authority. Exercise convenience does not justify uncontrolled business, safety, or customer impact.

options.label: Reject the timing, select a safer staged or parallel exercise
options.feedback: Correct. Reject the timing, select a safer staged or parallel exercise, define an approved full-interruption objective and window, and require business and safety authority. Exercise convenience does not justify uncontrolled business, safety, or customer impact.

options.label: Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately
options.feedback: Changed fact: A service owner requests a full-interruption test during the busiest business day because the team is available. Why this answer fails: “Bypass the normal owner and apply a permanent broad restriction immediately” does not account for that changed condition. Corrected consequence: State that the test proves restoration procedure and some capacity, not independence from identity failure. Repair target: Changed outcome verified — The decision remains provisional until the changed dependency, enforcement result, and accountable evidence are verified.

transfer.hint: Trace the changed fact to the exact decision boundary, then identify the evidence needed before the outcome can be accepted.

retry.prompt: A tabletop resolves a network-loss inject by calling an engineer whose number is not in the plan. What should the exercise record?

options.label: Mark the inject passed because someone eventually reached the right engineer
options.feedback: The outcome depended on information absent from the plan and would not be repeatable by another team.

options.label: Ignore contact details because tabletops assess discussion rather than operational readiness
options.feedback: A tabletop can and should expose decision, role, and communication gaps within its stated objective.

options.label: Mark the documented communication path as failed, capture the workaround separately, assign an update, and retest it
options.feedback: Correct. Exercise success depends on the planned capability, not hidden personal knowledge.

retry.hint: Separate the participant’s personal workaround from evidence that the plan works.

takeaway: State that the test proves restoration procedure and some capacity, not independence from identity failure.
assumptions: The scenario is a bounded application of the canonical unit, not a universal threshold, legal conclusion, or vendor prescription.
Directed edges carry only their printed relation; proximity and shared color do not imply ownership, authorization, or chronology.
Acceptance applies only to the stated scope and retained evidence; unknown or excluded conditions remain explicit.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The decision graph preserves objective, exercise boundary, synthetic data, shared dependencies, business observation, evidence limits, blast radius, approval, and abort rules. Evidence strength and operational disruption are encoded together in authored cases rather than exposed as two independently selectable axes, so the mechanism is equivalent.

learningJob.plainExplanation: An exercise proves only what its form, scope, participants, dependencies, and disruption permit it to test. A tabletop can test decisions and coordination, while technical restoration, capacity, and production failover need stronger evidence.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: A comparison matrix would expose evidence strength and disruption across tabletop, simulation, parallel, and interruption tests; the current single path withholds that selection logic.
